## COPG v7.6.1

*Makes the per-app ANDROID_ID spoof consistent across every read path, and fixes a `getprop` that could leak the real value.*

### ANDROID_ID — consistent everywhere
*   **The `aid` spoof no longer disagrees with itself.** Before, an app could read the faked ANDROID_ID from the normal settings lookup but still get the *real* one through a direct provider `query`/`call`, or by reading `settings_ssaid.xml` — and that mismatch is itself a giveaway. The `aid` tag now spoofs the value in the system server at the source, so every read path returns the same ID. The **Hook Status** screen gained an ANDROID_ID consistency badge on the `aid` row so you can confirm it at a glance.

### getprop — matches the API
*   **A shelled-out `getprop` now returns the spoofed value.** Closed a case where a `getprop` run through a wrapped shell slipped past the spoof and exposed the real property, so the command line and the framework API agree again.

### Other
*   Stability and hardening fixes.

releases.body:
## COPG v7.6.0

*Android 17 support, a new one-tap Random Device identity, an Integrations dashboard, a stealthier CPU-spoof backend, and a batch of crash and compatibility fixes.*

### Android 17 — supported
*   **COPG now runs on Android 17 (SDK 37).** Earlier builds could boot-loop a phone on A17 as soon as a system-wide hook (CorePatch, Google Account, Wallpaper ID, locale, VPN-hide, and friends) tried to install. The v7878 engine is now built from source and made A17-safe, so those device-wide hooks arm cleanly on the new release. If you were stuck on A16 or had the system-server spoofs gated off, they're back on.
    *   *Engine A17 fix: big thanks to the **HMA OSS** developer for the engine fix that made this possible.*

### Random Device — new
*   **A one-tap random phone.** The device list has a new **Random** profile at the top: pick it and the app sees a complete, self-consistent made-up phone — brand, model, fingerprint and build fields that all match — instead of a specific preset. It sits alongside **This Device** as a pinned option in the device picker. **FREE.**
*   **Fresh identity every launch (`randid`).** With the new **Randomize IDs** switch on a package, every derived identifier that COPG can roll — ANDROID_ID, serial, GAID, App Set ID, IMEI, wallpaper ID — is re-rolled each time the app launches, so it looks like a brand-new device on every start rather than one stable fake. Pair it with the Random profile for a full rotation, or use it on any profile. **PRO**, stealth where the underlying spoof is stealth.

### Integrations dashboard — new
*   **See the tools COPG is working with.** A new **Integrations** sheet under Settings lists the root manager, the Zygisk implementation and optional helper modules (such as NoMount) that COPG detects, each with a live status — active, installed, or absent — and its version. If a helper is too old to use safely (an out-of-date NoMount), it's flagged **Update needed** with a tap-to-read explanation of what to do. Makes it obvious at a glance what's powering the module on your setup.

### CPU spoof — stealthier backend
*   **Hides the CPU swap from mount scanners (optional).** When the **NoMount** kernel module is installed, the per-app `/proc/cpuinfo` spoof now goes through NoMount's in-kernel path redirect instead of a bind mount — so it no longer shows up in the app's own `/proc/self/mountinfo` (the trace that some anti-cheats flag as tampering). Without NoMount, COPG falls back to the normal bind mount, unchanged. The on-boot foreground reconcile honors the NoMount backend too.
*   **Needs NoMount 2.2.0 or newer.** Older NoMount builds had a kernel freeze/panic bug, so COPG now uses the traceless redirect only on 2.2.0+ and automatically stays on the safe bind mount on anything older (the Integrations card flags a NoMount that's too old).

### Zygisk status — improved
*   **Correct Zygisk name and version in the System tab.** The System tab now reports the real Zygisk implementation (Zygisk Next, ReZygisk, BReZygisk), its version, and whether it's actually injecting vs merely installed — read straight from the daemon rather than guessed, so a misnamed or disabled variant is no longer reported wrong.

### GPU spoof — fixed
*   **No more crash on Android 16 / newer chips.** On ARMv8.5 devices (and newer ROMs that map system libraries with branch-target hardening), turning on the GPU spoof could crash an app at launch with a `SIGILL` — most visibly games that query Vulkan during start-up. The inline hook now keeps the required landing instruction at the patch site, so it's safe on every device. *(The GPU spoof stays resident/detectable and behind the use-at-your-own-risk gate — still never for competitive games.)*

### Concurrent Mic — fixed
*   **Turning it off no longer needs a reboot.** Disabling **Concurrent Mic** now takes effect live; previously the audio server couldn't read the toggle under SELinux, so the feature stayed on until the next reboot.

### CorePatch — fixed
*   **No more Samsung lock/reboot loop.** On some Samsung devices the signature-verification patch could trip a "device locked, try again in 3 days" / inactivity-reboot loop. The signature check is now scoped to the package installer only (not every signature comparison on the device), and the mis-triggered Samsung inactivity-reboot is handled, so the loop is gone.

### Other fixes
*   **SIM/carrier** — a shelled-out `getprop` of the carrier props now matches what the API reports (closes a `getprop`-vs-API mismatch for `sim`/`simx`).
*   **VPN hide** — reports the real underlying interface so a VPN-detector no longer sees a network-type mismatch; added an older-Android file-view layer for `vpnn`.
*   **Home** — tap the **Devices** / **Packages** stat cards to jump straight to that Library tab.

### Thanks
*   **Huge thanks to @PARADOXCODM** for testing roughly **20 Android 17 builds** back-to-back while we chased the boot loop — including having to **factory-reset his own device** after one of our builds bricked the boot. A17 support in this release exists because of that patience. 🙏
*   Thanks to the **HMA OSS** developer for the v7878 engine fix behind the Android 17 support.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

**Kernel extensions.** A new `kernel.sh` covers the areas this module had not touched: devfreq bus and memory-controller clocks, KSM deduplication, transparent hugepages, `schedtune` boost, the full three-value TCP buffers, touch boost, and the filesystem ceilings (inotify, file-max, nr_open). **Config versioning.** Config writes now go through a temp file and an atomic rename rather than `sed -i`, so an interrupted write can no longer leave a half-written file. **SELinux.** The module now ships `sepolicy.rule` with 184 rules covering the nodes it writes. Previously some writes could be silently blocked on enforcing devices.

**Watchdog.** `watchdog.sh` checks autopilot, guard, appwatch and wipeshield every five minutes and restarts anything that died. They used to fail silently.

**Also**
- periodic TRIM, interval in days
- switch to powersave automatically below a battery level you choose
- dry run now reports what the kernel extensions would change
- WebUI: kernel extension switches, watchdog controls, devfreq listing

**Fixed**
- safe mode appended `SAFEGUARD=0` to the config, creating a duplicate key. It rewrites in place now
- the boot-failure counter was left as an empty file when cleared

Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

This build is mostly about the things that were missing rather than new switches on top of old ones.

**Config export and import** - everything you have configured (options, per-app rules, custom parameters, whitelist) goes into one JSON file on your storage. Import merges rather than replaces, so keys the backup does not contain are left alone. Useful when moving to a new device or sharing a setup.

**CPU frequency limits** - the profiles used to change the governor and nothing else. They now set scaling_max_freq and scaling_min_freq too, snapped to frequencies your kernel actually advertises. Ranges are 10-45 percent for powersave up to 60-100 for gaming.

**Range checking for custom parameters** - if a node has min and max files next to it, a value outside that range is refused before it is ever written. There is a force option if you know what you are doing.

**LMK and memory pressure** - min_free_kbytes scaled by installed RAM, lowmemorykiller minfree per profile, watermark tuning. This is usually the real reason background apps get killed, and it was not covered before.

**ZRAM sizing** - if zram0 has no size yet it gets 75 percent of RAM, with mkswap and swapon. Existing sizes are left alone.

**Thermal zone selection** - unlocking thermal no longer disables every zone blindly. You choose which ones, cpu and gpu by default. A new zones command lists every zone with its type, mode and temperature.

**Autopilot** - follows the system battery saver and can force a profile during a time window, including windows that cross midnight.

Everything from earlier versions is still there: four profiles, adaptive switching, charge limiting, app standby management, per-app policies, display tuning, boot-failure rollback, wipe protection and the WebUI, now with 8 tabs.

**CPU frequency limits** - profiles now set scaling_max_freq and scaling_min_freq, not just the governor. The range is picked from the frequencies your kernel actually exposes, so nothing is hardcoded. Toggle with the CPU 频率上下限 switch.

**Boot-failure rollback** - the module counts boots. If the system does not come up three times in a row, it rolls back every kernel and custom parameter it changed, writes the disable flag and turns itself off. This is what protects you when a custom parameter turns out to be wrong.

**Wipe protection** - a new guard with three modes:
- 增强模式: kills the process the moment a wipe command is seen
- 普通模式: pauses and asks you first, through the WebUI
- 不防护: logs only

It watches running processes and boot scripts for rm -rf on system paths, mkfs, dd to block devices, fastboot wipe/erase/format and shred. Temporary paths such as /tmp, /cache and /data/local/tmp are deliberately left alone.

Also: updateJson is now set, so the manager can tell you about new versions.

Everything from before is unchanged: four profiles, adaptive switching, charge limiting, app standby management, per-app policies, custom parameters, display tuning, initrc services and the WebUI.

First public release.

- Every preinstalled app is matched against a built-in safety list and labelled Safe, Careful or Required
- Apps the system depends on are refused outright, so a bad tap cannot break the boot
- Disable, hide (keeps all data) or freeze apps, one at a time or in bulk, per Android user
- Snapshots: a snapshot is taken automatically before any batch change, and restoring one only turns apps back on
- Review tab groups preinstalled apps by consequence, with bulk actions per group
- Background permissions per app: run in background, wake lock, start at boot, clipboard, overlays, usage access, installing other apps
- Battery policy per app: standby bucket and the Doze whitelist
- Backups to Download/APEX with the app files and, optionally, its data
- Dual apps and second space are handled as separate users
- A change journal with a one-tap undo of the last change
- Action button prints a summary of everything changed so far

Nothing is changed at install time. Requires a WebUI-capable root manager.
releases.name: v1.0.0

releases.body:
# Changelog

## 0.2.1-Stable - 2026-10-26

### Play Integrity

- Fetch selectable Pixel release fingerprints from Google build metadata, with
  Pixel 6a selected by default. Preview candidates and save their source metadata
  without applying them or enabling the engine. Leave unknown patch dates unset.
- Add quick controls for Build, property and Play Store fingerprint overrides.
  Explain the Play Store SDK compatibility mode and its precedence over fingerprints.
- Preview system, vendor and boot patch policies separately while retaining
  unselected partition settings and backend-specific formats.
- Persist process restart and device reboot requirements across page reloads.
  Keep independent keystore recovery available when an activation marker fails.
- Compare process-local Build and property snapshots with the saved configuration,
  matching revision, boot identity, PID and process start time. Import decoded
  integrity reports as unverified summaries; missing labels remain unknown.
- Extend configuration, recovery, JNI and mobile browser regression coverage,
  including narrow English, Chinese and right-to-left layouts. Local diagnostics
  and tests do not establish a Google Play Integrity verdict.

### Translations

- Add Ukrainian and Polish translations and localize the new integrity controls.

## 0.2.0-Stable - 2026-10-24

### Integrity and keystore compatibility

- Keep OEM lock-state and AVB property changes in their appropriate boot stages,
  including when Play Integrity is disabled, unconfigured or falls back after a failure.
- Validate SHA-256/SHA-512 boot hashes against backend requirements before saving.
  Preserve independent OhMyKeymint trust settings when only the prop handler changes.
- Serialize keystore configuration writes, restore failed updates, retain unknown
  default and per-app policy fields, and reject stale configuration or backend selections.
- Keep unsaved property and policy edits across background refreshes. Add explicit
  property reload and report settings that require a reboot.
- Align module disable/remove handling across the CLI, shell and native companion.
  Reject invalid compatibility options consistently without changing saved enable intent.
- Respect separate system, vendor and boot patch values when preparing optional
  keystore synchronization. Retain explicit configurations and skip incompatible
  single-date updates.

### Device provisioning

- Add MediaTek SoC detection, AIDL V1 RKP support and TrustKernel device-ID
  provisioning while retaining Qualcomm-specific defaults and backend selection.
- Refuse contradictory platform evidence and retain diagnostics for failed native
  provisioning. Firmware support and successful hardware issuance remain device-specific.

### Verification

- Extend configuration rollback, lifecycle, native/JVM, contract and mobile WebUI
  regression coverage, including API 36 AVD checks with KernelSU 3.3.0 and
  OhMyKeymint 1.2.0-b12557c.
- Local tests and emulator behavior do not establish Google Play Integrity verdicts
  or physical-device TEE, fingerprint and display compatibility.

## 0.1.8-stable - 2026-10-24

### Play Integrity

- Integrate a separately built Play Integrity Fork-derived engine with an opt-in
  configuration workflow, generation of Pixel Canary candidates, compatibility
  controls, diagnostics and history. Candidate generation and local configuration
  do not guarantee any Google Play Integrity verdict.
- Preview changes before applying configuration or optional keystore patch policies.
  Support structured field editing, raw import/export, saved profiles, migration,
  rollback, and confirmation before recovering an interrupted update.
- Make engine activation and emergency disable independent from configuration reads,
  including during errors and pending cleanup. Restore managed state when disabling.
- Improve phone-sized layouts: consistent navigation, panels, editor controls and
  preview alignment. Preserve drafts while switching tabs and correct Back behavior.

### Reliability and updates

- Paginate command history and diagnose empty backend responses.
- Handle different fingerprint-generator output paths and improve its diagnostics.
- Fall back to an English release download link when a Telegram ZIP exceeds the
  Bot API's upload limit.

### Licensing and verification

- Keep the derived engine under GPLv3 with upstream notices, and retain the
  independently implemented management interface under MIT.
- Link to the immutable build commit for corresponding source rather than
  embedding a duplicate source archive in the module.
- Add independent engine compilation, packaging checks, contract tests and
  mobile WebUI regression coverage to CI.

## 0.1.7-stable - 2026-10-19

### Tricky Store manager

- Accept EC-only keyboxes for OhMyKeymint while retaining certificate-chain and
  certificate-count validation for every supplied key.
- Preserve legacy and modern Xposed module detection with zip 9 through exact
  central-directory path lookups, including APKs with non-UTF-8 filenames.

### Dependencies

- Upgrade zip to 9.0.4 and refresh Rust and WebUI dependencies and lockfiles.

## 0.1.6-stable - 2026-10-18

### WebUI

- Run shell commands through the host's queued job API when available, so slow
  commands no longer block return navigation. Preserve output, exit status and
  compatibility with hosts that only provide `exec`.
- Stop restarting failed automatic update checks on each return to the home page;
  keep manual retries and channel changes available. Read the fixed hosting module
  identity once per WebUI session.
- Reduce target-list reconstruction overhead with shallow query snapshots, stable
  drafts and lightweight selection indicators. Measure new virtual rows through
  ResizeObserver to avoid repeated forced layout, including with enlarged text.
- Clean up command callbacks on completion and launch failures, including hosts
  that report a companion error after a nonzero exit.

## 0.1.5-stable - 2026-10-18

### WebUI

- Virtualize target and system-app lists while preserving search, bulk selection,
  keyboard focus and per-app controls. Batch synchronous package metadata lookups
  and stop queued lookups when their query is cancelled.
- Preserve edits made during target saves, update the saved baseline without an
  extra package-manager query, and guard overlapping writes.
- Keep RKP navigation available during loading, prevent overlapping profile
  operations, and discard results for changed inputs.
- Fix cached Device ID form initialization, language-switch races, cancelled file
  reads and malformed repository messages. Bound uploads and translation requests.
- Adapt buttons, tabs, forms, menus, dialogs and sheets to narrow screens, landscape
  and enlarged text. Wrap technical values and application names, improve supporting
  text size and contrast, and respect display safe areas.

## 0.1.4-stable - 2026-10-17

### RKP Workbench

- Add **Import DICE materials** as the main workbench entry, with separate offline
  validation, diagnostic CSR construction and online issuance commands. An existing CSR
  is not required; device collection and firmware patching are not implemented here.
- Preserve the imported chain, match explicit signing material to its leaf key, and
  construct a new CSR v3 using a fresh server challenge and newly generated attestation key.
- Share issuance and export between imported material and the labelled experimental
  degenerate-chain mode. Remove implicit offline fallback and successful error results.
- Select returned chains by public key, verify certificate signatures and constraints,
  and publish private keyboxes atomically after XML readback checks. JSON results contain
  paths and summaries instead of private XML. Installation remains independent.
- Bump the workbench feature contract to 2. Old profiles retain their seed derivation;
  material import does not overwrite profiles or an installed keybox.
- Accepts the integer DICE mode allowed by the `android.14` profile.
- Verification uses generated synthetic keys and a local simulated server. Real-material
  production acceptance and successful production export remain unverified for this path.

### Device RKP Issuer
- Automatic mode tries V2, AIDL V1 and native V1 in order, skipping unavailable methods.
  Any issuance or validation failure advances to the next method with a fresh challenge;
  failures are aggregated only after every method fails. Successful results include an
  attempt history. Local file writes happen after certificate validation succeeds.
- Adds the `v1-native` backend for vendor command `0x311e`. Native V1 reuses the
  V1 CSR assembler, structural checks and isolated worker, and does not require a system
  AIDL APK at runtime. Firmware and server acceptance remain unverified.
- Reports protocol and backend separately, exposes native V1 resource availability,
  and uses feature contract 5 across the CLI and WebUI.
- Adds the V1 AIDL signing oracle for Qualcomm PureSoft firmware with a zero HBK,
  adapted from LazyBonesLZY/rkp-v1-oracle under its MIT license.
- Adds automatic and explicit V1/V2 protocol selection.
- Selects the full EEK chain for the HAL's reported curve and uses the device's AIDL
  proxy in an isolated process, with bounded exchange files and timeout cleanup.
- Reports V1 as structurally checked; encrypted signing evidence is verified by the
  provisioning server. V2 retains local signature verification.
- Cross-checks Qualcomm aliases (including QTI/QCOM), SoC part numbers, hardware properties
  and kernel SoC information. Unknown and conflicting evidence have separate blockers;
  empty properties no longer imply support. The WebUI shows the evidence and keeps firmware
  and server compatibility unverified.
- Recognizes QTI as Qualcomm and gives the isolated worker vendor library search paths,
  retaining the default namespace's system dependency links for libraries such as libcrypto.
- Preserves worker error types and accepts bare as well as field-61-wrapped CSRs.
- Bounds exchange-file reads, rejects nonregular files and symlinks, and requires exactly
  one nonempty certificate chain for the requested key.
- Reserves private output directories atomically, removes partial runs on write failure,
  and saves keyboxes and private keys with mode `0600`, including explicit output copies.
- Uses the prerequisite report's device fingerprint consistently; an explicit fingerprint
  can satisfy a missing fingerprint without bypassing other prerequisites.
- Corrects the key export description: the exported keybox includes a software-generated
  private key; this path does not extract a private key from the TEE.

### TEE Attestation Extractor
- New offline tool for extracting Keybox XML and PEM material from existing captures and
  verifying private-key correspondence, certificate signatures and chain completeness.
- Verifies candidate RKP identity material against the signing leaf of a locally verified
  CSR, with separate Ed25519-seed, P-256-seed and P-256-scalar modes and raw capture offsets.
- Returns summaries without exposing private material. Explicit exports use private output
  directories and owner-only files; mismatched identity material cannot be exported.
- Adds binary uploads, device file paths, manager installation through an extension point,
  and translations in all 14 languages. Device-side acquisition is not included.
- Local checks do not establish root trust, revocation status, registration or server acceptance.
  Supported private keys are EC P-256/P-384 and RSA 2048–8192; RSA-1024 is unsupported.
- Verifies private-key PEM labels against their DER encoding. Inline inputs are limited
  to 32 KiB per file to fit shell transport; device file paths accept up to 256 KiB.
- Finds XML document boundaries through parsed tags, accepts closing-tag whitespace,
  and rejects illegal XML characters before exporting material.
- Rejects trailing data in CSR CBOR items, including embedded signed payloads, protected
  headers, DICE subject keys and configuration descriptors.
- Resolves same-name certificate issuers by signature and handles self-issued key rotation
  certificates without treating them as self-signed roots.
- Ignores root-tag examples in XML comments outside the captured document.

### WebUI
- Keeps long error details, links and code within the viewport.

### Command wrapper
- Preserves backend failure exit codes and tries fallback binaries only after execution
  failures (`126` or `127`).

## 0.1.3-stable - 2026-10-17

### Device RKP Issuer
- New tool: signs a P-256 key we generated with this device's Qualcomm KeyMint TA
  (`CSR_V2`, command `0x3122` over `libkeymasterdeviceutils.so`) and submits the resulting
  `AuthenticatedRequest` to Google's RKP server, then exports `keybox.xml` plus its private
  key. The request does not extract a private key from the TEE.
- Warns twice before it can run, and the backend refuses a run without
  `--acknowledge-limitations`: only some devices work, and only RKP certificates can be
  issued.
- Checks Android arm64, root, `/dev/smcinvoke`, `libkeymasterdeviceutils.so` and a Qualcomm
  SoC first, and reports exactly which prerequisite is missing.
- Validates the device's CSR (DICE chain, signature, challenge, `keysToSign`) and binds the
  issued certificate chain to the generated key before writing anything. The chain must also
  be one leaf-to-root path with no certificate left off it. These local shape and key

- Clean up command callbacks on completion and launch failures, including hosts
  that report a companion error after a nonzero exit.

## 0.1.5-stable - 2026-10-18

### WebUI

- Virtualize target and system-app lists while preserving search, bulk selection,
  keyboard focus and per-app controls. Batch synchronous package metadata lookups
  and stop queued lookups when their query is cancelled.
- Preserve edits made during target saves, update the saved baseline without an
  extra package-manager query, and guard overlapping writes.
- Keep RKP navigation available during loading, prevent overlapping profile
  operations, and discard results for changed inputs.
- Fix cached Device ID form initialization, language-switch races, cancelled file
  reads and malformed repository messages. Bound uploads and translation requests.
- Adapt buttons, tabs, forms, menus, dialogs and sheets to narrow screens, landscape
  and enlarged text. Wrap technical values and application names, improve supporting
  text size and contrast, and respect display safe areas.

## 0.1.4-stable - 2026-10-17

### RKP Workbench

- Add **Import DICE materials** as the main workbench entry, with separate offline
  validation, diagnostic CSR construction and online issuance commands. An existing CSR
  is not required; device collection and firmware patching are not implemented here.
- Preserve the imported chain, match explicit signing material to its leaf key, and
  construct a new CSR v3 using a fresh server challenge and newly generated attestation key.
- Share issuance and export between imported material and the labelled experimental
  degenerate-chain mode. Remove implicit offline fallback and successful error results.
- Select returned chains by public key, verify certificate signatures and constraints,
  and publish private keyboxes atomically after XML readback checks. JSON results contain
  paths and summaries instead of private XML. Installation remains independent.
- Bump the workbench feature contract to 2. Old profiles retain their seed derivation;
  material import does not overwrite profiles or an installed keybox.
- Accepts the integer DICE mode allowed by the `android.14` profile.
- Verification uses generated synthetic keys and a local simulated server. Real-material
  production acceptance and successful production export remain unverified for this path.

### Device RKP Issuer
- Automatic mode tries V2, AIDL V1 and native V1 in order, skipping unavailable methods.
  Any issuance or validation failure advances to the next method with a fresh challenge;
  failures are aggregated only after every method fails. Successful results include an
  attempt history. Local file writes happen after certificate validation succeeds.
- Adds the `v1-native` backend for vendor command `0x311e`. Native V1 reuses the
  V1 CSR assembler, structural checks and isolated worker, and does not require a system
  AIDL APK at runtime. Firmware and server acceptance remain unverified.
- Reports protocol and backend separately, exposes native V1 resource availability,
  and uses feature contract 5 across the CLI and WebUI.
- Adds the V1 AIDL signing oracle for Qualcomm PureSoft firmware with a zero HBK,
  adapted from LazyBonesLZY/rkp-v1-oracle under its MIT license.
- Adds automatic and explicit V1/V2 protocol selection.
- Selects the full EEK chain for the HAL's reported curve and uses the device's AIDL
  proxy in an isolated process, with bounded exchange files and timeout cleanup.
- Reports V1 as structurally checked; encrypted signing evidence is verified by the
  provisioning server. V2 retains local signature verification.
- Cross-checks Qualcomm aliases (including QTI/QCOM), SoC part numbers, hardware properties
  and kernel SoC information. Unknown and conflicting evidence have separate blockers;
  empty properties no longer imply support. The WebUI shows the evidence and keeps firmware
  and server compatibility unverified.
- Recognizes QTI as Qualcomm and gives the isolated worker vendor library search paths,
  retaining the default namespace's system dependency links for libraries such as libcrypto.
- Preserves worker error types and accepts bare as well as field-61-wrapped CSRs.
- Bounds exchange-file reads, rejects nonregular files and symlinks, and requires exactly
  one nonempty certificate chain for the requested key.
- Reserves private output directories atomically, removes partial runs on write failure,
  and saves keyboxes and private keys with mode `0600`, including explicit output copies.
- Uses the prerequisite report's device fingerprint consistently; an explicit fingerprint
  can satisfy a missing fingerprint without bypassing other prerequisites.
- Corrects the key export description: the exported keybox includes a software-generated
  private key; this path does not extract a private key from the TEE.

### TEE Attestation Extractor
- New offline tool for extracting Keybox XML and PEM material from existing captures and
  verifying private-key correspondence, certificate signatures and chain completeness.
- Verifies candidate RKP identity material against the signing leaf of a locally verified
  CSR, with separate Ed25519-seed, P-256-seed and P-256-scalar modes and raw capture offsets.
- Returns summaries without exposing private material. Explicit exports use private output
  directories and owner-only files; mismatched identity material cannot be exported.
- Adds binary uploads, device file paths, manager installation through an extension point,
  and translations in all 14 languages. Device-side acquisition is not included.
- Local checks do not establish root trust, revocation status, registration or server acceptance.
  Supported private keys are EC P-256/P-384 and RSA 2048–8192; RSA-1024 is unsupported.
- Verifies private-key PEM labels against their DER encoding. Inline inputs are limited
  to 32 KiB per file to fit shell transport; device file paths accept up to 256 KiB.
- Finds XML document boundaries through parsed tags, accepts closing-tag whitespace,
  and rejects illegal XML characters before exporting material.
- Rejects trailing data in CSR CBOR items, including embedded signed payloads, protected
  headers, DICE subject keys and configuration descriptors.
- Resolves same-name certificate issuers by signature and handles self-issued key rotation
  certificates without treating them as self-signed roots.
- Ignores root-tag examples in XML comments outside the captured document.

### WebUI
- Keeps long error details, links and code within the viewport.

### Command wrapper
- Preserves backend failure exit codes and tries fallback binaries only after execution
  failures (`126` or `127`).

## 0.1.3-stable - 2026-10-17

### Device RKP Issuer
- New tool: signs a P-256 key we generated with this device's Qualcomm KeyMint TA
  (`CSR_V2`, command `0x3122` over `libkeymasterdeviceutils.so`) and submits the resulting
  `AuthenticatedRequest` to Google's RKP server, then exports `keybox.xml` plus its private
  key. The request does not extract a private key from the TEE.
- Warns twice before it can run, and the backend refuses a run without
  `--acknowledge-limitations`: only some devices work, and only RKP certificates can be
  issued.
- Checks Android arm64, root, `/dev/smcinvoke`, `libkeymasterdeviceutils.so` and a Qualcomm
  SoC first, and reports exactly which prerequisite is missing.
- Validates the device's CSR (DICE chain, signature, challenge, `keysToSign`) and binds the
  issued certificate chain to the generated key before writing anything. The chain must also
  be one leaf-to-root path with no certificate left off it. These local shape and key
  checks do not establish certificate trust, revocation status or server acceptance.

## 0.1.2-stable - 2026-10-11

### Tricky Store manager
- Complete port of Tricky Addon (Update Target List):
  - Target list with modes, per-app policy, search, bulk selection, DenyList, unnecessary
    apps, system apps and auto-add.
  - Keyboxes from AOSP, "unknown", a local file, the keybox repository and custom providers,
    with import and export.
  - Prop settings, default policy with *Today*, help, keyboard shortcuts and its 23
    translations, including right-to-left languages.
- One manager for Tricky Store (`config.ini` and legacy `target.txt`), TEESimulator
  (`config.json`) and OhMyKeymint (`config.toml` + `injector.toml`).
  - The validation rules follow each module's own sources.
  - Unknown sections, comments and keys are preserved.
- Optional WebUI entry on the keystore module (plus the action button on Magisk), and the
  TSupport-Advance auto-target stop flag.
- Tricky Addon's in-app translation update, translation guide and Telegram link.
- Checked against the real modules on a KernelSU device, which found and fixed:
  - OhMyKeymint v1.2.0 rejected our `injector.toml` (an unknown `version` key) while the
    WebUI reported success. `[scoop.<package>]` tables are now read and written like
    OhMyKeymint's own parser does.
  - The "unknown" keybox now gives each key a two-certificate chain. Tricky Addon's
    single-certificate keybox only loads on Tricky Store: TEESimulator and OhMyKeymint
    refuse it.
  - TEESimulator accepts EC-only keyboxes, such as the RKP workbench exports.
  - Saving tells when OhMyKeymint needs a restart to apply a change.

### WebUI
- Rebuilt on Vue 3.5, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn-vue.
  - A black and white theme, light or dark, where color only marks errors, success and
    warnings.
  - Designed for phones along Material 3 Expressive:
    - 48dp touch targets and a visible response to every press.
    - Round buttons that square up while pressed, segmented lists, and spring motion.
    - A large title that collapses into the 64dp app bar, for one-handed reach.
    - Tonal gray surfaces instead of borders and shadows, with contrast checked
      against WCAG.
  - Menus, tabs and button groups mirror in right-to-left languages too.
  - Follows the KernelSU manager's window insets.
  - The Android back gesture closes dialogs and sheets.
- Every tool in 14 languages: English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean,
  Spanish, French, German, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Vietnamese and
  Indonesian.
- Help: long links and code wrap inside the page, and two slips in upstream translations
  (a link missing its parenthesis, a code span closed with a quote) no longer show raw
  Markdown.
- Every tool is a self-contained feature folder, discovered automatically.
  - Features plug into each other only through extension points.
  - Every backend response is validated against a schema.
- A tool whose backend feature is missing or on another contract version is disabled
  instead of misreading data.
- Unit tests (Vitest) and end-to-end tests (Playwright against a mock KernelSU host) with
  light, dark, right-to-left and Chinese screenshots.
- Contract tests run every API call through `duckctl.sh` and a real `duckd` build and
  parse the results with the WebUI's schemas.
- Device tests (`scripts/device-test.sh`) drive the WebUI inside the real KernelSU manager
  with each keystore module installed.
- Loads as seven files instead of about eighty. The KernelSU manager reads each request
  through a root shell, so this halved the load time on a slow device.
- Type-checked on the TypeScript 7 engine through typescript-native-bridge.

### Backend
- `duckd` builds its CLI from a feature registry. `duckd features` reports the compiled-in
  features, and each feature can be built alone.
- New `system` feature: module and device summary, stable and canary updates with changelog,
  output files, command history, uninstall and reboot.
- RKP profiles read their device defaults from AOSP build properties.
- Updated RustCrypto to its current generation (p256/p384 0.14, ed25519/x25519 3, aes-gcm
  0.11, x509-cert 0.3). Keys derived from saved seeds are pinned by regression tests.

### Module
- Scripts follow the KernelSU module guide:
  - Late-load support (`late-load.sh`).
  - A late prop pass after boot for values the system sets late.
  - The module description goes into KernelSU's temporary config.
- Magisk runs the boot-completed work from `service.sh`.
- The prop handler adds `ro.boot.vbmeta.size`, and applies the boot hash even when the
  handler is disabled, as upstream does.
- Uninstalling removes entry links, flags and saved data.

### Tooling
- CI fails when any source file in any language exceeds 600 lines.
- CI: NDK r30, Node 24, pnpm 12, WebUI lint/format/unit/E2E, per-feature builds.
- Canary artifacts are the installable module directory.
- Dependabot opens one pull request per major update.

# KernelSU-Tailscaled v2.0.5

Fix standalone Android control-plane connectivity and update the official
Tailscale engine directly from the module WebUI.

## Android connectivity

- Bundle official Tailscale 1.104.2, including upstream standalone Android DNS,
  network monitoring, and CA support.
- Native Android mode selects the official interface-binding implementation
  (`TS_FORCE_LINUX_BIND_TO_DEVICE=true`). Control and UDP sockets no longer
  depend on an absent main-table default route for marked traffic. No copied
  default routes, hard-coded control hosts, or patched engine binaries.
- Restrict login DNS diagnostics to actual login states; ordinary startup is
  no longer treated as evidence of a fresh-login DNS failure.

## Update the engine from WebUI

Open **Tailscale engine update** in the module dashboard, check for an official
stable release, download and verify it, then explicitly apply it. Downloading
alone leaves the running service untouched. Applying briefly restarts the
module's service; it does not reboot Android or require signing in again.

- ARM and ARM64 downloads use the official HTTPS stable server and published
  SHA-256 checksum, with bounded downloads and restricted archive extraction.
- Activation preserves identity and configuration, validates service recovery,
  and restores the previous engine/state if activation fails.
- Interrupted transactions recover on the next lifecycle operation. A later
  stop or disable is respected; recovery does not silently override it.
- Separately updated engines survive module updates and boot; a newer bundled
  engine takes precedence. Downgrades are rejected by the normal updater.

## Validation

- Real Xiaomi test: temporarily ran 1.102.3, then checked, downloaded, verified,
  and applied 1.104.2 using the same controller actions as WebUI. The running
  executable changed to the downloaded engine; identity/configuration stayed
  unchanged, and public peer connectivity recovered. Normal runtime restored.
- OnePlus: updated engine retained across a module reinstall and authorized
  reboot, with automatic service activation.
- Automated coverage includes checksum/archive rejection, rollback, interrupted
  activation, disabled/stopped intent, and browser check/download/apply flow.
- See `docs/verification/2026-10-22-release-2.0.5.md` for evidence and limits.

The reporter's exact ROM and complete fresh-account browser authorization are
not yet verified. ARM32 packages are checked, but phone runtime testing is ARM64.

## Install

Install the universal or architecture-specific ZIP through KernelSU Manager.
Existing v2 identity and configuration are retained. Reopen Details after an

# KernelSU-Tailscaled v2.0.5

Fix standalone Android control-plane connectivity and update the official
Tailscale engine directly from the module WebUI.

## Android connectivity

- Bundle official Tailscale 1.104.2, including upstream standalone Android DNS,
  network monitoring, and CA support.
- Native Android mode selects the official interface-binding implementation
  (`TS_FORCE_LINUX_BIND_TO_DEVICE=true`). Control and UDP sockets no longer
  depend on an absent main-table default route for marked traffic. No copied
  default routes, hard-coded control hosts, or patched engine binaries.
- Restrict login DNS diagnostics to actual login states; ordinary startup is
  no longer treated as evidence of a fresh-login DNS failure.

## Update the engine from WebUI

Open **Tailscale engine update** in the module dashboard, check for an official
stable release, download and verify it, then explicitly apply it. Downloading
alone leaves the running service untouched. Applying briefly restarts the
module's service; it does not reboot Android or require signing in again.

- ARM and ARM64 downloads use the official HTTPS stable server and published
  SHA-256 checksum, with bounded downloads and restricted archive extraction.
- Activation preserves identity and configuration, validates service recovery,
  and restores the previous engine/state if activation fails.
- Interrupted transactions recover on the next lifecycle operation. A later
  stop or disable is respected; recovery does not silently override it.
- Separately updated engines survive module updates and boot; a newer bundled
  engine takes precedence. Downgrades are rejected by the normal updater.

## Validation

- Real Xiaomi test: temporarily ran 1.102.3, then checked, downloaded, verified,
  and applied 1.104.2 using the same controller actions as WebUI. The running
  executable changed to the downloaded engine; identity/configuration stayed
  unchanged, and public peer connectivity recovered. Normal runtime restored.
- OnePlus: updated engine retained across a module reinstall and authorized
  reboot, with automatic service activation.
- Automated coverage includes checksum/archive rejection, rollback, interrupted
  activation, disabled/stopped intent, and browser check/download/apply flow.
- See `docs/verification/2026-10-22-release-2.0.5.md` for evidence and limits.

The reporter's exact ROM and complete fresh-account browser authorization are
not yet verified. ARM32 packages are checked, but phone runtime testing is ARM64.

## Install

Install the universal or architecture-specific ZIP through KernelSU Manager.
Existing v2 identity and configuration are retained. Reopen Details after an
update to load the new WebUI. The withdrawn beta.1 is not a supported release.

## 4.0.5 (4.0.4 → 4.0.5)

### Highlights

- Added a KernelSU module package containing the supported KMI builds and userspace checker. It detects the device KMI, enables boot auto-load by default, and provides an Action button and multilingual WebUI for module controls and checker output.
- Added KernelSU Manager update metadata (`update.json`) and automated publication of versioned module assets, the checker, and the KernelSU ZIP. Release tags are checked against the module version; release creation accepts an HTTPS URL for release notes.
- Hardened controlled unload and hot-reload around live namespace and IPC state. The module tracks vendored namespace proxies, namespace-filesystem inode pins, IPC objects, and deferred cleanup; unsafe teardown is refused until references and work drain. Diagnostic resource counters help identify remaining blockers.
- Added procfs lookup fallbacks for `/proc/<pid>/ns/ipc` and `/proc/<pid>/ns/pid` when native namespace entries are unavailable, including an Android 17 / 6.18 path using that KMI's procfs PID accessor.

### Compatibility and testing

- The QEMU workflow exercises the checker before and after module load, namespace/procfs behavior, container workloads, and post-use module unload using pinned official Google GKI images across eight KMIs: `android12-5.10`, `android13-5.10`, `android13-5.15`, `android14-5.15`, `android14-6.1`, `android15-6.6`, `android16-6.12`, and `android17-6.18`.
- KernelSU ZIP and release packaging require a complete supported-KMI build matrix.
- `NET_NS` remains bookkeeping-only; use host networking (`--network=host`). The module must match the device's exact KMI. On Android data filesystems with casefold support, configure Docker to use `fuse-overlayfs` as described in the user guide.

### Changes

**fix:**
- Improved namespace/IPC lifetime handling, task-exit cleanup, and Android 5.10 compatibility; fixed KernelSU install permissions and shell invocation of control scripts.

**docs and licensing:**
- Added consolidated `copying.txt` terms to the project and KernelSU package, with clarified attribution and provenance metadata.

## v1.4.10 — NetBird v0.81.3
- Optimized the status watcher: one shared `status --json` call per cycle (was up to three netbird CLI spawns) with the module.prop description now parsed from JSON, and an idle mode while the client is disconnected — route re-checks and watchdog restarts are skipped and the cycle relaxes to `NB_IDLE_UPDATE_INTERVAL` (default 300s), so a downed client costs almost nothing. `webui up` starts a dead daemon on demand (detached, with auto-connect) and refreshes underlay routes immediately on reconnect.
- Added confirmed connection controls to the WebUI overview: Reconnect/Disconnect (fast daemon-IPC `up`/`down` reusing persisted flags) and Start/Stop daemon. Daemon lifecycle runs detached (`nohup`) with the page polling status, so closing the WebUI cannot interrupt it; every control requires a confirmation dialog. New fixed `webui` service actions: `up`, `down`, `daemon-start`, `daemon-stop`.
- Fixed the WebUI misreading a disconnected client as a stopped daemon: netbird's `daemonStatus` reports the connection state, so the page now tracks process state and connection state separately. After `webui down` the banner shows "disconnected" (with the stop/start controls intact) instead of switching to the start-daemon card; Connect/Disconnect buttons disable according to the current connection state and a needs-login state is surfaced.
- Restyled WebUI notices as centered translucent-gray toasts with rounded corners.
- Silenced the 5-second refresh cooldown on implicit loads (tab switches no longer pop an "updated recently" toast), deduplicated concurrent identical commands, and added a background Networks prefetch so the first Networks view renders instantly.
- Tab switches now render the destination view with its loading placeholder first and defer the data read until the slide transition finishes (240ms), removing the animation stutter caused by firing the root-command bridge mid-transition; stale timers are ignored when switching again quickly.
- Fixed the English "Refresh system routes"/"Refresh runtime rules" labels overflowing their two-column action buttons (shortened copy plus wrapping allowed in the action grid).
- Implicit-load failures now surface in-page instead of as toasts: Networks shows an error placeholder with retry, diagnostics show the error in the output area, and status-bridge errors appear as a detail line inside the banner. Toasts are reserved for explicit switch/confirm actions.
- When the daemon is stopped, views drop cached rows and show a "daemon is stopped" placeholder (Networks and Peers), and no doomed read commands are fired; the Networks cache is invalidated the moment status reports the daemon stopped, so stale rows never survive inside the 5-second cooldown.
- A running-but-disconnected client no longer triggers the raw "failed to list network: not connected" error: Networks shows a friendly not-connected placeholder (or a connecting indicator), the route rows and bulk enable/disable actions are hidden outside the healthy state, and the doomed `networks list` call is skipped; remaining error messages drop the CLI's "Error: " prefix.
- Fixed the watchdog restart path: `kill "$pid"2>/dev/null` was missing a space, so TERM/KILL targeted a nonexistent PID and a wedged daemon was never actually killed before the restart attempt.
- Deduplicated the busybox-timeout wrappers in the status watcher (`nb_with_timeout`) and made `client_cmd` delegate to `webui_client`.
- Removed the WebUI forwarding-rules view: NetBird dropped the `forwarding` CLI command in v0.81.0 together with management-side ingress ports, so the view always failed with `unknown command "forwarding"`.
- The `webui forwarding` service action now returns an explicit "no longer available in NetBird v0.81.0+" error instead of passing the raw CLI failure through, so stale cached WebUI pages show a clear message.
- The Networks view now shows a loading state while retrying after a failed load, matching the removed forwarding view's behavior.
- Moved the WebUI bridge sources (`view-model.mjs`, `kernelsu.js`) out of `module/webroot/` into `ui/src/`, so the shipped webroot contains only build output; removed the duplicate `ui/src/lib/utils.ts` and two unused i18n strings.
- Install-time extraction now skips the `update.json` / `updates/*.json` download manifests (managers fetch updates via the `updateJson` URL in `module.prop`, so the copies in `MODPATH` were dead weight).

## NoMount v2.2.0 is here!🎉

This release brings UID-scoped rules, opaque directory redirection, `.remove` support, and the biggest hot-path optimization pass we've ever shipped. The kernel driver and the metamodule **must be updated together**.

> Commit count hit 605 on this release. Driver protocol is now v22. Thanks to everyone who kept reporting, bisecting and testing through the rough week 💙

### Small Changelog:

- kernel/:
  - Wire protocol v22. `nm_rule_hdr` grew from 16 to 24 bytes and `nm_del_hdr` from 10 to 18 to fit the new UID range fields. A v22 CLI cannot talk to a v21 driver (and vice versa); the installer aborts if the running driver is older than v22.
  - UID-scoped rules with ranges: `--uid-range 1000-5000` and `--uid-range all`. A single rule now covers a whole range without enumerating every UID.
  - UID deny sub-ranges: `--uid-excluded 3000-4000`. Combine it with `--uid-range` for `[1000,5000] except [3000,4000]`, or use it alone as "default except this range". Rules with the same target range but different denies are rejected with `-EEXIST`; overlap between ranges is rejected too.
  - Opaque directories: `--opaque`. A directory rule can hide the underlying filesystem entirely and only expose the module's leaves. This is what `.replace` with content actually meant: previously it whiteouted the whole directory and bootlooped when the hidden dir was a system app the framework needed.
  - Pseudo filesystems (`proc`, `sysfs`, `devpts`, `debugfs`, `tracefs`, `selinuxfs`, `cgroup`, `bpf`) are no longer hijacked at the dentry level.
  - Skip d_op installation on dentries that have no rule for their name. This is the biggest change in the release: it removes the d_revalidate tax on every non-rule lookup under a hijacked directory, which is most of them.
  - Skip d_op installation on dentries in pseudo filesystems, and skip the `shrink_dcache_parent` pass when invalidating a single injected name. The `nm_hijack_dentry_ops` publication now uses `smp_store_release` and a single `d_flags` write.
  - Hot-path micro-optimizations, reorder `nm_dir_ops` so the hot fields fit in one cache line, avoid `current_fsuid()` when the leaf is NULL, skip `nm_is_uid_blocked()` and `nm_find_leaf_in_dir()` when there is no leaf or no children, short-circuit `nm_dir_lookup` and `nm_d_revalidate_common` on directories without rules.
  - `nm_d_revalidate_common` no longer reads `dentry->d_op` or `inode->i_op` when it does not need them, and chains to the original `d_revalidate` when the underlying filesystem has one.
  - On unload, walk `i_dentry` to clear `d_op` before freeing module memory. Fixes the panic on `rmmod` with files open on virtual paths.
  - `iget5_locked` hits no longer allocate an `nm_inode_info`; the probe uses a stack struct and `kmalloc` only happens for `I_NEW`. `d_add` instead of `d_splice_alias` for fresh file inodes.
  - Probe `xattr_handler->__get` via header grep instead of `LINUX_VERSION_CODE`, so kernel trees that never backported the member compile again.
  - `inode_state_read_once` for I_NEW checks (mainline >=6.19 compatibility).
  - Deferred reclaim of rules and leaves moved fully to process context. `nm clear rules` no longer blocks on `synchronize_rcu`.
  - Internal naming unified to the `nm_` prefix.

- userspace/:
  - `--uid-range <a>-<b>`, `--uid-range all`, `--uid-excluded <c>-<d>`, and `--opaque` flags.
  - `nm rule list` prints `[UID: a-b excl c-d]` and emits `"opaque": true` in the JSON output.
  - Streamlined absolute path handling, chunked output for large rule lists.

- module/:
  - `common.sh` holds the boot pipeline: bootloop detection keyed on `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, LKM loading, module disable. `post-fs-data.sh` and `metamount.sh` are thin wrappers over it.
  - Boot order is now correct on both KernelSU and APatch. The previous flow silently lost rules on APatch (and sometimes in KernelSU with specific setups) because metamount.sh ran before the LKM was loaded.
  - Bootloop detection no longer relies on `.booting` existence; a successful boot clears the file, a failed boot keeps the boot_id and the next boot disables the module.
   - `.remove` support: Magisk's .remove marker is recognized alongside `.replace` (`.replace` with content → opaque rule, `.replace` alone → whiteout, `.remove` → whiteout).  `rule-paths.sh` gains `path`, `pair`, `opaque` and `del` kinds, and both `metamount.sh` and the WebUI's hot load/unload use the same flow. Hot unload now deletes opaque rules too.
  - `x86_64` build support: new CI matrix entry, `lkmloader-x86_64`, `nm-x86_64`, and `ARCH_BIN` normalization for KernelSU's `x64` label.
  - Installer aborts if the running driver is below v22, and falls back to the previous LKM if a v22 KO is staged for the next boot. Reboot is required to activate the new driver in LKM mode.

- webui/:
  - Skip / Unskip button on each module card (creates or deletes `skip_mount`).
  - Persist the "Show system apps" toggle across reloads.
  - Back gesture closes the right dialog in every navigation state (fixed double back navigation).
  - AMOLED palette adjustments and clear button corner fix.

and a lot of other misc changes :)

#### Thanks to everyone who kept testing, contributing and reporting through the rough bits: @ZQZCC, @nleloc, @sohan-f, and the testers on the Telegram group 🫂

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/maxsteeel/nomount/compare/v2.1.1...v2.2.0

```text
这次把 FuseHide 的 FUSE 缓存失效调度收紧了喵。原来根目录 entry、指定 entry 和 inode 失效会按请求创建 detached 线程，大量目录项同时被过滤时容易堆积线程；线程还会持有原始 fuse_session 指针，MediaProvider 销毁 session 后存在继续访问旧指针的风险喵（尾巴警觉地竖了起来）

Native 这边改为进程内共享的单 worker 和有界任务队列，保留原来的 entry 25 ms、根目录 entry 和 inode 50 ms 延迟，并对排队中的同类目标去重。队列最多容纳 4096 个任务，超出时限制警告日志频率并拒绝继续入队，避免高负载下无上限地消耗线程与内存喵（一个一个来，不许偷偷分身）

生命周期方面新增 fuse_session_destroy 的 ELF 导入槽 Hook，兼容文件映射与 APK 内嵌 ELF 的安装路径。销毁前先阻止新任务、清空待执行队列，再等待正在执行的通知退出；新 session 被识别时更新代际并清理旧的跟踪状态。未能安装销毁 Hook 时不安排异步通知，避免继续使用无法保证生命周期的 session 指针喵（认真守住销毁顺序）

```
